rule: rust-workspace-architecture checklist — Errors: "Is a Result in a new Drop, event handler or fire-and-forget path observed somewhere?" / audit scope: "cleanup skipped on the error path", "inconsistent handling of the same condition in two places"
summary: One unreadable or non-git worktree directory aborts the entire startup recovery scan, so every later repository's attempts are left unrecovered and post-create hook intents are never reconciled.
failure_scenario: A user has two repos registered. Under `worktrees/acme/api/` there is a directory `feature-a` left behind with a `.git/fleet-creating.json` marker but a broken `.git` (e.g. a stale `gitdir:` pointer after a manual `mv`, or `git` transiently unavailable). On daemon start, `recover_published("feature-a")` reaches `git.current_branch` → `Err` → `RecoveryValidity::Unavailable` → `recover_startup` returns `Err` at line 27. `schedule_startup_recovery` (recovery.rs:109-114) only logs `"publish-intent recovery scan failed"` and sets `startup_ready`. Consequences: (a) every remaining directory in that repo and every directory of the second repo is never recovered — worktrees that finished their rename but not their state write stay invisible to the daemon while occupying their canonical path, so the next `create` for that slug fails with `worktree destination already exists`; (b) `recover_post_create_intents()` at line 31 never runs, so post-create hooks interrupted by the restart are neither relaunched nor recorded as `degraded`, and their intent files accumulate in `cache/post-create/` forever.
proposed_fix: Make the per-child loop failure-isolating the way `recover_attempt` already is: replace `self.recover_published(&repo, name, &child).await?` with a match that logs the error at `tracing::warn!` and continues (and do the same for the `recover_attempt` call, whose remaining `?` paths are `worktree_id`/`files.rename`/`files.trash`). Keep `recover_post_create_intents()` outside the loop so it always runs, and only propagate errors that indicate the whole scan is impossible (`config.load`, `state.load`).
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees.rs`'s `mod tests`, add `startup_recovery_survives_one_unobservable_worktree`: using `fixture()`, register two repos; under repo A create `worktrees/acme/api/broken/` containing `.git/fleet-creating.json` but configure the `FakeShell` so `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` in that path exits non-zero; under repo B create `worktrees/acme/web/good/` with a valid marker and a shell that reports the matching branch; also write one `cache/post-create/<id>.json` intent for a registered worktree. Call `service.recover_startup().await`. Before the fix the call returns `Err`, `good` is absent from `state.worktrees`, and the post-create intent file still exists; after the fix `recover_startup` returns `Ok(())`, `good` is registered, and the intent has been consumed.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees/recovery.rs:25-31 — both per-child calls use `?` inside the repo loop, and `recover_post_create_intents()` sits after the loop, so any Err aborts the whole scan. recovery.rs:201 `RecoveryValidity::Unavailable(error) => return Err(error)` is reachable: recover_published only bails early when the marker is unreadable (recovery.rs:179-182), so a published dir that still carries `.git/swarm-creating.json` (crash between rename and marker removal, publication.rs:98) reaches `git.current_branch` (recovery.rs:226-230 -> adapters/git.rs:337 `branch --show-current`, `checked` errors on non-zero status). recover_attempt deliberately quarantines the identical condition and returns Ok (recovery.rs:151-155), so the two sites really do disagree. schedule_startup_recovery only logs (recovery.rs:109-114), and nothing else ever calls recover_post_create_intents (only post_create.rs:179 definition + recovery.rs:31 call site). No existing test covers a failing child: tests/worktrees_lifecycle.rs:229 and tests/reset_state.rs:96 both drive the happy path.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees/recovery.rs only; existing coverage in crates/fleet-daemon/tests/worktrees_lifecycle.rs:193-239 and crates/fleet-daemon/tests/reset_state.rs:96 must keep passing (they assert Ok + registration, unaffected). A new test belongs in the inline `mod tests` of crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees.rs (fixture() with FakeGit/FakeShell) rather than the integration test, which uses real git.
corrected_fix: The proposal is right in shape but under-specifies the swallow boundary. Isolate per-child: `if let Err(error) = self.recover_published(...).await { tracing::warn!(%error, path = %child.display(), "skipped worktree during startup recovery"); }` and the same for recover_attempt. Do NOT swallow the errors raised before the loop (config.load, state.load, reconcile_trash_expiries, migrate_legacy_remote_records) — a half-migrated legacy archive must still fail loudly. Also keep `recover_post_create_intents()` reachable even if the loop is later made fallible again (e.g. run it before returning any accumulated error), since it is the only reconciliation path for detached hooks.

rule: audit scope: "operations that are not idempotent on retry"; rust-workspace-architecture: "inconsistent handling of the same condition in two places" (the clone path solves this, the hook path does not)
summary: The detached post-create runner's pid is persisted only after the child is spawned, so a daemon crash inside that window makes startup recovery launch the user's post-create hooks a second time, concurrently with the first still-running copy.
failure_scenario: A repo has `postCreate: ["npm ci", "./scripts/seed-db.sh"]`. `fleet create` publishes the worktree, `schedule_post_create` submits the job, `launch_detached_post_create` spawns `sh -c RUNNER` (hooks start), and the daemon is killed (`make restart`, OOM, laptop sleep-kill) before line 102 writes the pid. The runner is detached and keeps going. On the next start, `recover_post_create_intents` reads the on-disk intent with `pid: None` and no status file, takes the `else` branch, and spawns a second `sh -c RUNNER` in the same worktree — two `npm ci` processes writing `node_modules` and two `seed-db.sh` runs against the same database. Both eventually `mv` their own `$tmp` over the same `FLEET_STATUS_PATH`, so the recorded exit code is whichever finished last, and `record_post_create_failure`/`clear_post_create_failure` mark the worktree from the wrong run.
proposed_fix: Make the runner publish its own identity before doing any work, as the clone wrapper already does: prepend `printf '%s\n' "$$" > "${FLEET_STATUS_PATH}.pid.tmp"; mv "${FLEET_STATUS_PATH}.pid.tmp" "${FLEET_STATUS_PATH}.pid"` to `RUNNER`, and have `recover_post_create_intents` treat the existence of that pid file (not just `intent.pid`) as proof the hooks already started — relaunching only when neither the pid file nor the status file exists. Alternatively write the intent with a `launching: true` marker before `spawn_detached_child` and never relaunch an intent that carries it.
test_plan: Add `interrupted_post_create_launch_is_not_relaunched` beside the existing worktree tests. Build a `Worktrees` over `fixture()`, write a `PostCreateIntent` into `cache/post-create/` with `pid: None`, a `status_path` that does not exist, and hooks `["touch $PWD/ran-$$"]`; have the runner's pid file already present on disk (simulating a spawn that happened before the crash). Call `recover_post_create_intents().await` and drain the job. Before the fix the `FakeShell` records a second `sh -c <RUNNER>` invocation; after the fix it records none and the job instead waits for/reads the status file.
verify_reason: post_create.rs:97-102 — spawn_detached_child (jobs/job.rs:111-122 -> shell.run_detached) starts the hooks, and only afterwards is `intent.pid` set and written. The intent already exists on disk with pid: None from run_detached_post_create (post_create.rs:66). Recovery keys purely on that (post_create.rs:216-222), and RUNNER writes FLEET_STATUS_PATH only as its last statement (post_create.rs:19-21), so a crash inside the window relaunches non-idempotent user hooks concurrently. The clone path really does solve it child-side (adapters/git.rs:135-143, plus a parent-side fallback write at git.rs:156-161). The existing test worktrees.rs:739 `post_create_crash_is_recoverable` asserts relaunch for pid: None — it does not distinguish 'never spawned' from 'spawned, pid unwritten', so it does not cover this. Caveat the finding overstates: the window is the few ms between run_detached returning and one atomic_write_text, against hook runs of minutes — severity is low, not high.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees/post_create.rs (RUNNER string, launch/finish/recover branches, PostCreateIntent if a field is added), fleet-core if PostCreateIntent lives there (it is serialized to cache/post-create/*.json, so an added field must be #[serde(default)] to keep old intents loadable), and the inline tests crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees.rs:739 and :795 which construct PostCreateIntent literally.
corrected_fix: Prefer the child-side variant that already exists for clone (adapters/git.rs:135-143): prepend `pid_file="${FLEET_STATUS_PATH}.pid"; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "${pid_file}.tmp"; mv "${pid_file}.tmp" "$pid_file"` to RUNNER and treat that file's existence as proof the hooks started. Do not use the 'launching: true' alternative alone — writing the marker before spawn turns every genuine spawn failure into a permanently unrecoverable intent (the hooks never ran but are never retried). Whichever is chosen, the recovery branch must fall back to the pid recorded in the pid file so finish_detached_post_create can still wait, and cleanup_post_create_intent (post_create.rs:163) must delete the new pid file too, otherwise cache/post-create leaks a second file per run.

rule: audit scope: "missing timeouts", "incorrect cancellation"; the daemon already models process identity as pid+start time (crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/process.rs:30-41) and this path ignores it
summary: After a daemon restart the post-create reconciliation job busy-waits on a raw pid from the previous boot with no start-time check, no timeout and no cancellation, so a recycled pid pins the job — and its dedupe key — forever.
failure_scenario: The machine reboots while a post-create runner is mid-flight. The persisted intent carries `pid: 4711`. After the reboot pid 4711 has been handed to `systemd-journald` (owned by root, so `kill(4711, 0)` returns `EPERM` and `pid_is_alive` says true). `recover_post_create_intents` takes the `intent.pid.is_some()` branch and `finish_detached_post_create` spins on `pid_is_alive(4711)` every 50 ms for the life of the daemon. The job stays `Running` forever, its `(JobKind::PostCreateHooks, <worktree id>)` entry stays in `JobManager::in_flight_targets` (crates/fleet-daemon/src/jobs/manager.rs:332-337 returns the existing id for a matching target), so every subsequent post-create job for that worktree silently dedupes into the wedged one and never runs, and the worktree's `degraded` field is never cleared or set.
proposed_fix: Persist the child's start identity alongside its pid (the daemon already computes `ProcessIdentity` in `adapters/process.rs`) and treat a pid whose start identity no longer matches as dead. Additionally give the wait a bound: pass the `JobCtx` into `finish_detached_post_create` and replace the bare loop with `tokio::select!` on `context.cancel.cancelled()` plus a deadline after which the intent is resolved as "runner did not record completion" via the existing `record_post_create_failure` path. Submit the reconciliation job as cancellable.
test_plan: Add `recovered_post_create_does_not_wait_on_a_foreign_pid` in the worktrees test module. Write an intent whose `pid` is `1` (init: always alive, never ours) with a `start_identity` that cannot match, no status file, for a registered worktree. Run `recover_post_create_intents().await` and await the job under `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), ...)`. Before the fix the timeout elapses with the job still `Running`; after the fix the job finishes and the worktree carries `degraded.kind == "post_create_hooks"`.
verify_reason: post_create.rs:110-114 is an unbounded `while pid_is_alive(pid) { sleep(50ms) }` with no deadline and no cancellation; pid_is_alive (adapters/process.rs:159-166) reports true for any foreign process, including EPERM-only ones. The recovery job is submitted with JobPolicy::new(false, false) (post_create.rs:214; manager.rs:76 signature is (cancellable, retryable)), and finish_detached_post_create takes no JobCtx, so nothing can interrupt it. The dedupe consequence is real: manager.rs:332-337 and :358-360 return the existing id for a matching (kind, target), so a wedged PostCreateHooks job swallows every later one for that worktree. The daemon does model identity as pid+start_identity elsewhere (adapters/process.rs:29-42), so the asymmetry is genuine. Pid recycling itself is the speculative half; the missing bound is not.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees/post_create.rs (finish_detached_post_create signature, both call sites at :100 and :217-219, PostCreateIntent serde shape if a start marker is persisted), and the inline test crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees.rs:795 `successful_retry_clears_degradation`, which calls finish_detached_post_create directly and would need the new argument. Making the reconciliation job cancellable also changes what fleet job cancel exposes (jobs/manager.rs record.cancellable) and any snapshot golden that includes job records.
corrected_fix: Persisting ProcessIdentity is heavier than the finding implies — DetachedProcess carries only a pid, so the start identity would have to be sampled with a Process::snapshot right after spawn, which races the child's own exit and adds a platform dependency. The proportionate fix is the bound, not the identity: (1) give the wait a deadline (e.g. a few minutes past the last mtime change of intent.log_path, or a flat cap) and on expiry take the existing record_post_create_failure path with 'detached hook runner did not record completion' — the same message post_create.rs:110-120 already uses; (2) treat the status file as the authority — poll `files.exists(&intent.status_path)` alongside pid liveness and stop as soon as it appears; (3) pass JobCtx in and select! on context.cancel.cancelled(), submitting with JobPolicy::new(true, false). Only add start-identity matching afterwards if the pid-reuse case is actually observed.

rule: audit scope: "cleanup skipped on the error path", "inconsistent handling of the same condition in two places"
summary: If a card is archived while its worktree is being cloned, `create_and_link_worktree` returns the generic archived-card refusal and drops the worktree it just created on the floor, unlike the adjacent branch that explicitly names the orphan.
failure_scenario: A user presses `w` on card `ENG-14`; the clone takes ninety seconds (`Worktrees::create` copies the pristine base and runs prepare hooks). Mid-clone the user archives the card. When `create` returns, the reload finds `archived == true` and the function returns `cannot create a worktree for an archived card`. The worktree is fully published and registered in `state.worktrees` with its session, its directory and any post-create hooks, but no card references it and the message the user sees claims nothing was created — the identical message they would have seen had they pressed `w` on an already-archived card. The only trace is `fleet list`.
proposed_fix: Give the archived branch the same shape as the card-gone branch: when `made` is present (i.e. the clone actually ran) return a `Conflict` that names the created worktree — e.g. `format!("worktree {} was created, but its card was archived", made.1.id)` — so the two post-clone failure paths report consistently. Keep the bare `archived_card()` only for the pre-clone check at worktree.rs:94-96.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/boards/tests.rs`, add `archiving_a_card_during_the_clone_names_the_created_worktree`: call `create_worktree_from_card_routed` with a `create` callback that, before returning `Ok((true, worktree))`, archives the card through `update_card`. Assert the returned error message contains the worktree id. Before the fix the message is exactly `cannot create a worktree for an archived card`; after the fix it names the orphan, and the test additionally asserts the worktree is still present in `state.worktrees` so the reporting change is the contract.
verify_reason: The code is exactly as quoted: boards/worktree.rs:180-197 returns the generic archived_card() after `made` exists, while the immediately preceding card-gone branch (:181-190) deliberately names the orphan and carries a comment explaining why. So the inconsistency is real and the author of the sibling branch clearly considered this class. But it is a message-quality issue, not a defect: no state is corrupted, the worktree is registered and reachable via fleet list exactly as the card-gone branch leaves it, and reusing the shared refusal constant may well be intentional. I cannot prove a defect from the code alone, and severity is at most cosmetic.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/boards/worktree.rs:196 and any test asserting the exact refusal string — crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/boards/tests.rs and crates/fleet-daemon/tests/boards_service.rs both match on messages; the pre-clone check at worktree.rs:94-96 must keep the bare archived_card() text so its assertions stay valid.
corrected_fix: If changed at all, branch on made.0 rather than assuming a fresh clone: Worktrees::create is idempotent and reports whether it actually made one (see the comment at worktree.rs:205), so the message must not claim 'was created' when an existing worktree was adopted — e.g. `if made.0 { Conflict(format!("worktree {} was created, but its card was archived", made.1.id)) } else { archived_card() }`. The same caveat applies to the existing card-gone branch at worktree.rs:185-189, which already claims 'was created' unconditionally; fixing one and not the other just moves the inconsistency.
